title: Genesis capital was paired with an election to distribute 5% of token supply between years ten and thirty
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.4.1 and .2 each set an Initial Allocation of 25,000,000 USDS, and A.2.8.2.2.2.4.3 links it to a token commitment: "The Initial Allocation is distributed in USDS to each Prime SubProxy... Both Grove and Spark elected to distribute 5% of the total token supply over a period of 20 years, lasting from year 10 to year 30, and will receive USDS 25,000,000 each."

The pairing implies a genuine choice was on offer — an election, with the cash allocation attached to taking it. On ten billion tokens, 5% is 500 million tokens per Prime, released between years ten and thirty.

The timing is the striking part. The distribution begins after the ten-year USDS user reward schedules in A.2.8.2.2.2.1.2.2.1 and .2 have finished, so the two programmes are sequential rather than overlapping. Token emissions therefore continue for three decades in total, with a long tail that starts precisely as the front-loaded incentives end.

Economically, the Prime trades a distant and heavily discounted claim on 5% of its own supply for 25 million USDS today. That is a rational exchange for an entity with immediate operating needs and no treasury, and it is cheap for Sky, which pays cash now against dilution that lands a decade out.

A.2.8.2.2.2.4.6 attaches a safeguard by reference — "Each genesis capital allocation is subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop" — and A.2.8.2.2.2.7.2 conditions the transfer on Surplus Buffer funding being approved, "ensur[ing] that capital deployment is aligned with the successful launch of the Prime's token and the commencement of its independent operations." The cash is released against a launched token, not against a promise.
description: Spark and Grove each receive 25 million USDS to their SubProxy, having elected a 5% supply distribution running over twenty years starting a decade out.
